:::{#def-lbfgs}
#### Limited-memory BFGS (L-BFGS)

**Limited-memory BFGS** (**L-BFGS**)
[@nocedal2006numerical, Chapter 7]
is the [quasi-Newton method](#def-quasi-newton-method)
that never forms $\matr{H}^{(t)}$.
It stores only the $m$ most recent pairs $(\vecf{s}^{(j)}, \vy^{(j)})$,
with $m$ small, such as $5$ or $20$,
and obtains $\matr{H}^{(t)} \deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t)})$
by applying the [BFGS update](#def-bfgs-update) for those $m$ pairs to a simple starting [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix), such as a multiple of $\matr{I}_p$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-lbfgs-cost}
#### Why L-BFGS is used for large problems

BFGS stores a dense $p \times p$ [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) and spends about $p^2$ operations per iteration.
L-BFGS stores $2m$ vectors with $p$ entries each and spends about $m p$ operations per iteration,
so it remains usable when $p$ is in the thousands or millions,
as in fitting a regularized logistic regression with many predictors.

:::
